rag.name: FiniteDimensional.basisSingleton
rag.content:
/-- In a vector space with dimension 1, each set {v} is a basis for `v ≠ 0`. -/
@[simps repr_apply]
noncomputable def basisSingleton (ι : Type*) [Unique ι] (h : finrank K V = 1) (v : V)
    (hv : v ≠ 0) : Basis ι K V :=
  let b := Module.basisUnique ι h
  let h : b.repr v default ≠ 0 := mt Module.basisUnique_repr_eq_zero_iff.mp hv
  Basis.ofRepr
    { toFun := fun w => Finsupp.single default (b.repr w default / b.repr v default)
      invFun := fun f => f default • v
      map_add' := by simp [add_div]
      map_smul' := by simp [mul_div]
      left_inv := fun w => by
        apply_fun b.repr using b.repr.toEquiv.injective
        apply_fun Equiv.finsuppUnique
        simp only [LinearEquiv.map_smulₛₗ, Finsupp.coe_smul, Finsupp.single_eq_same,
          smul_eq_mul, Pi.smul_apply, Equiv.finsuppUnique_apply]
        exact div_mul_cancel₀ _ h
      right_inv := fun f => by
        ext
        simp only [LinearEquiv.map_smulₛₗ, Finsupp.coe_smul, Finsupp.single_eq_same,
          RingHom.id_apply, smul_eq_mul, Pi.smul_apply]
        exact mul_div_cancel_right₀ _ h }

/-- If `ι` is an empty type and `V` is zero-dimensional, there is a unique `ι`-indexed basis. -/

    (hV : finrank K V = 0) : Basis ι K V :=
  haveI : Subsingleton V := finrank_zero_iff.1 hV
  Basis.empty _

prescopes: variable {α : Type} [DecidableEq α] {X Y : Set α} [∀ a, Decidable (a ∈ X)] [∀ a, Decidable (a ∈ Y)]
informal_statement: If you have a set of columns that are linearly independent and you take any subset of these columns, the subset will also be linearly independent.
informal_proof:
We are given that a set of columns \( J \) in a matrix \( B \) is linearly independent over the field \( \mathbb{Z}_2 \). We need to show that any subset \( I \) of \( J \) is also linearly independent.

Assume for contradiction that \( I \) is not linearly independent. Then, there exist coefficients in \( \mathbb{Z}_2 \) (either 0 or 1) that are not all zero, such that a linear combination of the columns in \( I \) equals the zero vector. However, since \( I \) is a subset of \( J \), any linear combination of columns in \( I \) is also a linear combination of columns in \( J \). Given that \( J \) is linearly independent, this would imply that the only solution is the trivial one, where all coefficients are zero. This contradicts our assumption that there exists a non-trivial linear combination equal to zero. Therefore, our initial assumption is false, and \( I \) must be linearly independent.

Thus, any subset of a linearly independent set of columns is also linearly independent.

id.name: Matrix.indepCols_subset
id.content:
/-- A subset of a linearly independent set of columns is linearly independent. -/
theorem Matrix.indepCols_subset {B : Matrix X Y Z2} (I J : Set α) (hBJ : B.IndepCols J) (hIJ : I ⊆ J) :
    B.IndepCols I := by
  obtain ⟨hJ, hB⟩ := hBJ
  use hIJ.trans hJ
  show LinearIndependent Z2 (fun i x => Matrix.fromCols 1 B x ((hJ.elem (Subtype.map id hIJ i)).toSum))
  apply hB.comp
  intro _ _ hf
  apply Subtype.eq
  simpa [Subtype.map] using hf

C1_dependencies.name: id
C1_dependencies.content:
/--
The identity function. `id` takes an implicit argument `α : Sort u`
(a type in any universe), and an argument `a : α`, and returns `a`.

Although this may look like a useless function, one application of the identity
function is to explicitly put a type on an expression. If `e` has type `T`,
and `T'` is definitionally equal to `T`, then `@id T' e` typechecks, and Lean
knows that this expression has type `T'` rather than `T`. This can make a
difference for typeclass inference, since `T` and `T'` may have different
typeclass instances on them. `show T' from e` is sugar for an `@id T' e`
expression.
-/
@[inline] def id {α : Sort u} (a : α) : α := a

C1_dependencies.name: Subtype.map
C1_dependencies.content:
/-- Restriction of a function to a function on subtypes. -/
@[simps]
def map {p : α → Prop} {q : β → Prop} (f : α → β) (h : ∀ a, p a → q (f a)) :
    Subtype p → Subtype q :=
  fun x ↦ ⟨f x, h x x.prop⟩

C1_dependencies.name: Matrix.fromCols
C1_dependencies.content:
/-- Concatenate together two matrices B₁[m × n₁] and B₂[m × n₂] with the same rows (M) to get a
bigger matrix indexed by [m × (n₁ ⊕ n₂)] -/
def fromCols (B₁ : Matrix m n₁ R) (B₂ : Matrix m n₂ R) : Matrix m (n₁ ⊕ n₂) R :=
  of fun i => Sum.elim (B₁ i) (B₂ i)
C1_dependencies.compilationAlias:

def fromCols (B₁ : Matrix m n₁ R) (B₂ : Matrix m n₂ R) : Matrix m (n₁ ⊕ n₂) R :=
  of fun i => Sum.elim (B₁ i) (B₂ i)
